questions: Are the repeated mouth, jaw, and tongue movements involuntary?
Did these movements begin suddenly?
Did they begin within the past 24 hours?
Have you recently developed weakness or numbness on one side of your body?
Are you having trouble speaking or understanding speech?
Have you had any loss of awareness or blackouts during these movements?
Can you temporarily suppress the movements?
Do you feel an urge or inner tension before they occur?
Have you taken an antipsychotic medication?
Have you taken metoclopramide, prochlorperazine, or another medicine for nausea?
Has any medication dose been increased or decreased recently?
Do you have Parkinson’s disease?
Do you take levodopa or another Parkinson’s medication?
Do you have similar involuntary movements in your arms, legs, or trunk?
Are you having difficulty swallowing?
Are you having difficulty breathing?
Have you had a recent head injury?
Have you recently used cocaine, amphetamines, or another stimulant?
Has anyone in your family had similar involuntary movements?
Have these movements been present for more than three months?
orders: Detailed neurologic examination, including assessment for chorea, dystonia, tics, tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia, cerebellar signs, and other abnormal movements during distraction and voluntary activation
Direct observation of the movements during speaking, counting, sustained tongue protrusion, rapid alternating movements, walking, and handwriting
Comprehensive medication, supplement, and toxin exposure review, including prior exposure to dopamine-blocking drugs

Peripheral blood smear and reticulocyte count

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Chronic spontaneous orofacial dyskinesia (non–drug-induced oro-bucco-lingual dyskinesia of aging)

ALTERNATIVE 1: Tardive dyskinesia from an unrecognized prior dopamine-receptor–blocking medication exposure

ALTERNATIVE 2: Edentulous dyskinesia related to dentures or loss of dental support

ALTERNATIVE 3: Orofacial dystonia (Meige syndrome)

1. Detailed neurologic examination, including assessment for chorea, dystonia, tics, tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia, cerebellar signs, and other abnormal movements during distraction and voluntary activation
